analysis: This PR is documentation-only. It changes docs/architecture/security/provider-trust.md (date bump at head line 3, new paragraph at head lines 128-136) and docs/developer/build.md (new SDK 27.2 Date-comparison section at head lines 180-192). No source, config, or enforcement code changes are in scope. I checked the new text against TB-011, TB-002, T-057 and the related authorization invariants. The new paragraph says a Date `>=`/`<=` weak-import crash loop on pre-release macOS 27.2 leaves App Attest pending and relaxes no authorization. That matches TB-011's rule that missing evidence and expiry do not extend basic policy or proof age, and that unavailable evidence is not an authorization fallback. It adds no new trust claim and no exception to attestation policy. The documented mitigations are scripts/check-date-comparisons.py in CI and scripts/check-provider-weak-imports.py at release build. The docs themselves note the first is syntactic and can miss comparisons, and the second reads the built binaries. This is a documented limit, not a regression. Those scripts and the provider Swift code that uses timeIntervalSince(_:) are not in the supplied evidence. I could not verify that the same thresholds and semantics are preserved, so I treated that as an unverified external contract and not a finding. The crash-loop availability impact on an affected Mac (T-057-like) is acknowledged in the text. One residual point for integration: the claim that the crash 'relaxes no authorization' depends on coordinator-side behavior, which the platform repo owns. It is consistent with existing TB-011 text, and no threat-model update is required.
